question: Does scaling an autoregressive language model to 175B parameters make task-agnostic in-context (zero-, one-, few-shot) learning competitive with fine-tuned systems?
hypothesis: Since in-context learning involves absorbing many skills and tasks within the parameters of the model, in-context learning abilities might show similarly strong gains with scale.
contributions: Train GPT-3, a 175B-parameter autoregressive LM (10x any previous non-sparse LM), and test it in zero-, one- and few-shot settings with no gradient updates
Train a family of 8 models from 125M to 175B to study scaling of in-context learning
Evaluate on over two dozen NLP datasets plus novel synthetic tasks (arithmetic, word scrambling, novel words, news generation)
Systematic data-contamination analysis with clean-subset re-evaluation
Preliminary bias, misuse and energy analysis

method.summary: GPT-2-style decoder-only transformers (with alternating dense and locally banded sparse attention) trained at 8 sizes from 125M to 175B on 300B tokens of filtered Common Crawl plus WebText2, Books1, Books2 and Wikipedia. Evaluated with no fine-tuning: K demonstrations placed in a 2048-token context (K=0, 1, or up to ~10-100), scoring multiple-choice by LM likelihood and free-form answers by beam search.
method.task: next-token pretraining; in-context (zero/one/few-shot) evaluation on NLP benchmarks and synthetic tasks

datasets.name: Common Crawl (filtered)
datasets.size: 410 billion tokens (60% of mix; 0.44 epochs elapsed in 300B tokens)
datasets.source: 41 shards of monthly CommonCrawl 2016-2019, 45TB compressed plaintext before filtering, 570GB after, roughly 400 billion BPE tokens
datasets.preprocessing: Logistic-regression quality classifier (Spark tokenizer + HashingTF) with WebText/Wikipedia/books as positives and raw Common Crawl as negatives; keep doc iff np.random.pareto(alpha) > 1 - document_score with alpha = 9; fuzzy dedup with Spark MinHashLSH, 10 hashes (dataset shrank ~10% on average); WebText fuzzily removed; partial benchmark 13-gram removal (buggy)

training.optimizer: Adam with beta1 = 0.9, beta2 = 0.95, epsilon = 1e-8; global gradient norm clipped at 1.0
training.lr: per model, 6.0e-4 (125M) down to 0.6e-4 (175B); see Table 2.1
training.lr_schedule: cosine decay down to 10% of its value over 260 billion tokens, then continues at 10% of the original learning rate
training.warmup: linear LR warmup over the first 375 million tokens
training.batch_size: 0.5M to 3.2M tokens by model size (Table 2.1); batch size increased linearly from 32k tokens to the full value over the first 4-12 billion tokens depending on model size
training.seq_len: 2048 tokens, multiple documents packed per sequence and delimited by an end-of-text token, no special masking
training.regularisation: weight decay 0.1; data sampled without replacement until an epoch boundary; higher-quality datasets sampled 2-3 times, CommonCrawl and Books2 less than once
training.hardware: V100 GPUs on part of a high-bandwidth cluster provided by Microsoft; model parallelism within each matrix multiply and across layers
training.compute: 3.64E+03 petaflop/s-days (3.14E+23 flops) for GPT-3 175B (Table D.1); 1 PF-day = 8.64e+19 flops

inference.decoding: free-form completion: beam search with beam width 4 and length penalty alpha = 0.6 (as in Raffel et al. 2019); multiple-choice: compare LM likelihood of each completion; bias probes and the poem samples: temperature 1, top p 0.9
inference.temperature: 1 (bias probes and Appendix F poems); not stated for task evaluation (beam search)
inference.top_p: 0.9 (bias probes and Appendix F poems only)
inference.samples: one evaluation per setting; K demonstrations randomly drawn per evaluation example from the task's training set (new draw per problem except WSC and MultiRC in SuperGLUE, which reuse one drawn set); Table C.1 scores use a different random seed for the in-context examples; news study: 5 outputs per title, the one closest in word count to the human article selected
inference.prompting: zero-shot: natural-language instruction only; one-shot: one demonstration plus description; few-shot: K demonstrations (typically 10 to 100, as many as fit in n_ctx = 2048), delimited by 1 or 2 newlines; K chosen on dev set from a few values when dev and test both exist; K=32 for SuperGLUE, K=100 for scramble tasks; per-task formats in Appendix G

parameters.multiple_choice_normalisation: per-token likelihood for most tasks; for ARC, OpenBookQA and RACE normalise by unconditional probability P(completion|context)/P(completion|answer context) with answer context 'Answer: ' or 'A: '
parameters.binary_classification: options given meaningful names (True/False) and treated as multiple choice
parameters.scoring: F1, BLEU or exact match depending on dataset
parameters.test_submission: only the 175B few-shot results submitted to test servers (SuperGLUE, TriviaQA, PIQA); dev set reported elsewhere

baselines: fine-tuned BERT-Large and BERT++ on SuperGLUE
eval.protocol: Single run per setting and model size; no confidence intervals on benchmark scores except an estimated std of 1.2% on the 1500-example ANLI R3 dev set. Contamination: clean subset = examples with no N-gram (N = 5th percentile example length, min 8, max 13) overlap with training data; compare clean vs all score. Human study: ~80 US participants per model via Positly, 25 articles, two-sample t-test (scipy.stats.ttest_ind) vs control; 621 of 718 recruited retained.

limits: Authors concede GPT-3 text samples repeat, lose coherence over long passages, contradict themselves and contain non-sequiturs; special difficulty with common-sense physics.
Does little better than chance on comparison tasks (WiC, ANLI, parts of reading comprehension, RTE/CB weak); conjectured due to autoregressive-only, unidirectional design.
No fine-tuning of GPT-3 was run; the fine-tuning setting is left to future work, and no bidirectional or denoising comparison at this scale.
Pretraining objective weights every token equally; poor pre-training sample efficiency; not grounded in other modalities.
Unclear whether few-shot learning learns tasks from scratch at inference time or only recognises tasks seen in training.
Inference at 175B is expensive and inconvenient; distillation at this scale untried.

Training-set contamination: a bug in the 13-gram filtering left overlaps, model not retrained; results on PIQA and Winograd marked with an asterisk; Wikipedia LM benchmarks and Children's Book Test unusable; clean subsets may differ in distribution from the full set.
Results mostly on a single run with random K-example draws; benchmark std not reported except ANLI (1.2%); test set results only submitted for SuperGLUE, TriviaQA, PIQA.

Hyperparameters not fully given: number of GPUs, wall clock, steps, precision format, dropout, vocabulary size and exact sparse-attention pattern are not stated; training code and weights not released.
Few-shot baselines compared to fine-tuned SOTA are not always comparable (translation uses 1 or 64 paired examples, supervised Fr-En/De-En SOTA the authors admit they may not know).
Bias analysis is preliminary, covering only gender, race and religion with co-occurrence methods.
Dated: the findings predate instruction tuning, RLHF and chat models; the Chinchilla-style compute-optimal ratio (300B tokens for 175B) was later revised.
